newsitem.title: POLAND: Fewer lay-offs help cut Polish April unemploment.
newsitem.headline: Fewer lay-offs help cut Polish April unemploment.

text.p: Fewer industrial lay-offs and more job offers pushed Poland's unemployment rate down to 12.4 percent in April from 13 percent in March, Labour Minister Tadeusz Zielinski said on Monday.
"We saw a further decline in the number people dismissed by enterprises... We also observed 104,000 job offers, 23,000 more than in March," Zielinski told a news conference.
He said the unemployment rate went down also because fewer school leavers registered themselves in April as unemployed.
In April, 2.13 million people were registered as unemployed, compared with 2.23 million in March and 2.67 million in April, 1996.
